title: information density: large containers render almost nothing, and storefront shows a single letter where a photo belongs
businessRules: An empty state exists to tell the operator what is missing and what to do next. A box that reserves 144px of a till screen to say one sentence fails that purpose even when the sentence is correct.

The box may be styled without its text being styled, and that is what happened: the POS and the storefront sized and coloured .emptyState but shipped no rule for the

and

inside it, so both rendered at browser-default size and margin. The Admin app had those rules; the other two did not.

A heading is a heading whichever element carries it. One real Admin empty state uses <h2> where the stylesheet only listed <h4>, and until h2 and h3 were listed it rendered unstyled inside the same 132px box that h4 handled correctly.
One line of text does not need a full panel, so a single-sentence empty state stops reserving the min-height reserved by icon-bearing ones.
The box is never filled with placeholder content to make it look busy. The fix is legibility and proportion, not invented data.
acceptanceCriteria: POS .emptyState and .syncEmpty style their h4, p, span, strong and small children; storefront .emptyState styles its h4 and p; Admin styles h2 and h3 as well as h4.
tests/operator-surface-completeness.test.mjs passes 10 of 10, pinning all three so the typography cannot be removed again.
npm run lint passes across all six workspaces and the full dependency-free suite is green.
testPlan: tests/operator-surface-completeness.test.mjs: source contract over the three stylesheets. It asserts the text rules exist and that the h2/h3 gap is closed.
Visual acceptance on a real till size is NOT done: whether 144px became 92px reads better is a judgement no source assertion can make.
migrationPlan: No database change. Stylesheet rules only.
rollbackPlan: Revert the commit. Four CSS rule blocks in three stylesheets, no runtime path, no data, no flag. Nothing to compensate.
monitoringPlan: The test runs inside npm run test:dependency-free and therefore in CI, so removing a rule again fails the build. No runtime metric applies: no server path changed.
securityNotes: Read-only presentation. No credential, personal data, permission, tenant scope, endpoint or input handling is involved; the change adds text-size and colour declarations and nothing else.
